read.thesis: Record $51B backlog (+71% y/y) and Power and Energy capacity adds point to supply expansion, but 2026 tariff cost rises to $2.6B and margins guided near bottom of range.

capex.quote: Capital expenditures are expected to be around $3.5 billion, driven primarily by our capacity expansion plans.

triggers.label: 2026 capex ~$3.5B for capacity
triggers.quote: Capital expenditures are expected to be around $3.5 billion, driven primarily by our capacity expansion plans.

triggers.label: Backlog $51B, up 71% y/y
triggers.quote: Our backlog grew to a record level of $51 billion, an increase of $21 billion or 71% compared to last year.

triggers.label: 2026 price realization ~2%
triggers.quote: We also expect all three segments to benefit from positive price realization, about 2% of total sales and revenues

triggers.label: Incremental tariffs $2.6B in 2026
triggers.quote: For the full year, incremental tariff costs are expected to be around $2.6 billion, which is $800 million higher than incurred in 2025.

guidance.quote: we anticipate full-year sales and revenues to grow around the top of the 5% to 7% long-term compound annual growth rate target
incremental tariff costs are expected to be around $2.6 billion
Capital expenditures are expected to be around $3.5 billion
MP and E free cash flow is expected to be slightly lower than 2025

guidance.value: near bottom of target range incl. tariffs
guidance.quote: Including the impact of tariffs, we expect margin to be near the bottom of the target range.

red_flags.label: Margin guided near bottom of range on tariffs
red_flags.quote: Including the impact of tariffs, we expect margin to be near the bottom of the target range.

red_flags.label: Backlog stretching beyond 12 months
red_flags.quote: approximately 62% of our backlog is expected to deliver in the next twelve months, which is lower than our historical average.

evasions.topic: Power gen capacity vs demand overbuild risk
evasions.quote: there could be puts and takes, forecasts move around
